# AWS Emulator Docker Image

> Unofficial, signed, multi-arch (linux/amd64, linux/arm64) container image of the AWS Emulator (https://github.com/aws/aws-emulator), a local emulator of the AWS APIs. Current upstream version: __VERSION__. Maintained by Yurii Serhiichuk (https://serhiichuk.dev). Not affiliated with Amazon Web Services.

AWS does not publish a prebuilt image. This project builds one from the pinned upstream RPM or DEB package. The build checks the package signature. The project tests the image on both architectures. It signs the image with cosign and adds an SBOM and SLSA provenance. A workflow checks for a new upstream release every hour. It publishes a new image in about one to two hours.

## Images

- `ghcr.io/xsavikx/aws-emulator`, `docker.io/xsavikx/aws-emulator`, `quay.io/xsavikx/aws-emulator`
- Tags: `latest`, `lts`, `__VERSION__` (package version), `__VERSION_SHORT__` (emulator version), `1.0`, `1`, immutable build tags `__VERSION__-<yyyymmdd>.<run>`; Debian variant with the `-debian` suffix and `debian`; distroless variant (no shell) with the `-distroless` suffix and `distroless`.

## Quick start

```sh
mkdir -p ~/.aws/emulator
docker run --rm --memory=2g --memory-swap=2g -p 127.0.0.1:9297:9297 \
  --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
  -e HOME="$HOME" -v "$HOME/.aws/emulator:$HOME/.aws/emulator" \
  ghcr.io/xsavikx/aws-emulator -p 9297
export AWS_ENDPOINT_URL=https://127.0.0.1:9297
export AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE=~/.aws/emulator/9297/emulator_credentials
export AWS_CONFIG_FILE=~/.aws/emulator/9297/config
export AWS_CA_BUNDLE=~/.aws/emulator/9297/ca.pem
export AWS_EC2_METADATA_DISABLED=true
export AWS_DISABLE_HOST_PREFIX_INJECTION=true
export AWS_REGION=us-east-1 AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=us-east-1
unset AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY AWS_SESSION_TOKEN AWS_PROFILE
aws sts get-caller-identity   # Account 000000000000
```

## Key facts

- Publish the port only on 127.0.0.1; the image binds 0.0.0.0 inside the container.
- Use the same port on the host, in the container and in the emulator `-p` argument.
- TLS uses a self-signed CA (`ca.pem`) that is new at each start. Node.js needs NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS; Rust and .NET need SSL_CERT_FILE; Java needs a truststore.
- Rootless Docker: use `--user 0:0`. Podman: `--userns=keep-id`.
- Use 127.0.0.1, not localhost, and path-style S3 addresses.
- AWS SDK for JavaScript v3: set `useQueueUrlAsEndpoint: false` on SQSClient, or SQS requests go to real AWS.
- Other containers cannot reach the emulator by service name: the certificate names only localhost, 127.0.0.1 and ::1.
- All state is in memory. Give the container 2 GiB.
- Verify the signature: `cosign verify ghcr.io/xsavikx/aws-emulator:latest --certificate-identity 'https://github.com/xSAVIKx/aws-emulator-docker/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/heads/main' --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com` (cosign v3 or later).

## GitHub Action

- [Run AWS Emulator on the GitHub Marketplace](https://github.com/marketplace/actions/run-aws-emulator): `- uses: xSAVIKx/run-aws-emulator@v1` starts the image, waits until healthy, and sets AWS_ENDPOINT_URL, credentials and CA variables for the next steps. Works on Linux runners with Docker or Podman, x64 and arm64. Use a `-debian` or `-distroless` tag in the `image` input for another variant.
